extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how to require restriction/election in patent applications (including election of species, linking claims, telephone practice, preparation of restriction requirement letters, and handling replies/traversals). Focused on examiner practice under 35 U.S.C. 121 and related CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate classification thereof
rubrics_metrics.description: This shows that each invention has attained recognition in the art as a separate subject for inventive effort, and also a separate field of search. Patents need not be cited to show separate classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use separate classification as a basis for requiring restriction; patents are not required to demonstrate separate classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate status in the art when classifiable together
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though they are classified together, each invention can be shown to have formed a separate subject for inventive effort when the examiner can show a recognition of separate inventive effort by inventors. Separate status in the art may be shown by citing patents which are evidence of such separate status, and also of a separate field of search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite patents or other evidence demonstrating recognized separate inventive effort or separate status in the art to justify restriction even if classification is the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different field of search
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is necessary to search for one of the inventions in a manner that is not likely to result in finding art pertinent to the other invention(s) (e.g., searching different classes/subclasses or electronic resources, or employing different search queries), a different field of search is shown, even though the two are classified together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The indicated different field of search must be pertinent to the subject matter covered by the claims; patents need not be cited to show different fields of search.

rubrics_metrics.name: No grounds for division when same classification/search and no indication of separate future classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the classification is the same and the field of search is the same and there is no clear indication of separate future classification and field of search, no reasons exist for dividing among independent or related inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If classification and search are the same and no evidence of separate status, do not require restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking claims — effect on restriction and rejoinder
rubrics_metrics.description: Linking claims are claims which, if allowable, would require rejoinder of otherwise divisible inventions. Linking claims and the inventions they link together are usually either all directed to products or all directed to processes; if a linking claim is allowable, restriction may be withdrawn and rejoinder required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 821.04 for rejoinder practice. Use appropriate form paragraphs when linking claims are present; identify linking claims and explain effect if they become allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of species required (general procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where restriction between species is appropriate the examiner should send a letter including only a restriction requirement or place a telephone requirement to restrict. Applicant should be required to elect a single disclosed species under 35 U.S.C. 121, and advised as to the requisites of a complete reply and his or her rights under 37 CFR 1.141.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action steps: (A) Identify generic claims or indicate none present. (B) Clearly identify each disclosed species (preferably by figures/examples or by mechanical means/material/distinguishing characteristic). Provide reasons why the species are independent or distinct. (C) Require election of a single disclosed species and advise regarding complete reply and rights under 37 CFR 1.141.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of a complete reply to an election of species requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to a requirement made according to this section should include a proper election along with a listing of all claims readable thereon, including any claims subsequently added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An argument that a claim is allowable or that all claims are generic is considered nonresponsive unless accompanied by an election. Election may be made with or without traverse; to preserve petition rights, election must be made with traverse and traversal must distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traversal and petition rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The election may be made with or without traverse. To preserve a right to petition, the election must be made with traverse. If the reply does not distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the election of species requirement, the election shall be treated as an election without traverse. Traversal must be presented at the time of election in order to be considered timely. Failure to timely traverse the requirement will result in the loss of right to petition under 37 CFR 1.144.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If traversing on the ground that species are not patentably distinct, applicant should submit evidence now of record showing obvious variants or clearly admit on the record. Examiner may use evidence/admission in a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection of the other species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of allowance of a generic claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the allowance of a generic claim, applicant will be entitled to consideration of claims to additional species which depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable generic claim as provided by 37 CFR 1.141.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing a generic claim can entitle applicant to rejoin additional species claims that depend from or require the generic claim limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs for linking claims and species restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should use form paragraph 8.12 to make restrictions involving linking claims when the linking claim is other than a genus claim linking species inventions. When the linking claim is a genus claim linking species inventions, examiners should use form paragraph 8.01 or 8.02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the correct form paragraph depending on whether linking claim is genus or other; include linking claim numbers and indicate 'between' or 'among' as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to restrict between linked inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application includes two or more otherwise properly divisible inventions that are linked by a claim which, if allowable, would require rejoinder, the examiner should require restriction, either by a written Office action that includes only a restriction requirement or by a telephoned requirement to restrict (the latter being encouraged).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If linking claim later indicated allowable, withdraw restriction and rejoin claims requiring all limitations of allowable linking claim; advise applicant about provisional double patenting concerns for continuation/divisional claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action on the merits following restriction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, when only a nonfinal written requirement to restrict is made, no action on the merits is given. A 1-month (not less than 30 days) shortened statutory period will be set for reply when a written restriction requirement is made without an action on the merits. The Office action making the restriction requirement final ordinarily includes an action on the merits of the claims of the elected invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone election of a single invention should be accompanied by a complete action on the merits of the elected claims. When preparing a final action where applicant traversed the restriction requirement, follow MPEP § 821.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for making a restriction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.142(a) indicates that a restriction requirement 'will normally be made before any action upon the merits; however, it may be made at any time before final action.' The examiner should make a proper requirement as early as possible in prosecution, in the first action if possible, otherwise as soon as need develops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before making restriction after the first action on the merits, examiner will consider whether there will be a serious burden if restriction is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone restriction practice (procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner determines that a requirement for restriction should be made, the examiner should formulate a draft and telephone the attorney or agent of record and request an oral election, with or without traverse, after the attorney or agent has had time to consider the restriction requirement. Arrange a second telephone call generally within 3 working days. If representative objects or fails to respond, mail a restriction letter referencing the unsuccessful call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an oral election is made, incorporate into the Office action a formal restriction requirement including date of election, attorney/agent name, a complete record of the telephone interview, followed by a complete action on the elected invention as claimed. Use form paragraphs 8.23 or 8.23.01 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require restriction if none of claimed inventions classifiable in examiner's Technology Center
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner should not require restriction in an application if none of the claimed inventions is classifiable in his or her Technology Center. Such an application should be transferred to a Technology Center wherein at least one of the claimed inventions would be examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If oral election would cause examination in another TC, initiate transfer with signed memorandum of restriction requirement and record of interview; differences resolved through supervisory chain of command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear and detailed record of restriction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must provide a clear and detailed record of the restriction requirement to provide a clear demarcation between restricted inventions so that it can be determined whether inventions claimed in a continuing application are consonant with the restriction requirement and therefore subject to the prohibition against double patenting rejections under 35 U.S.C. 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention particular claim limitations and reasons why such limitations support restriction; identify groups, give short descriptions, classification, and indicate disposition of every claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline of required elements in a restriction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The outline to set forth a requirement to restrict includes: (A) Statement of the requirement and identification of each group; (2) List claims in each group; (3) Short description of extent of subject matter claimed in each group; (4) Classify each group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also take into account claims not grouped (linking claims—identify and state possible group assignments; other ungrouped claims—indicate disposition); provide factual points showing independence/distinctness; provide reasons for insisting upon restriction and a summary statement advising as to reply required and effects of allowance/cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to insist upon restriction (enumerated bases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide reasons for insisting upon restriction: (1) Separate status in the art; (2) Different classification; (3) Same classification but recognition of divergent subject matter; (4) Divergent fields of search; or (5) Search required for one group not required for the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 8.14–8.20.02 as appropriate to elaborate the factual basis for these reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required conclusion paragraph for restriction requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: One of form paragraphs 8.21.01 through 8.21.03 must be used at the conclusion of each restriction requirement: 8.21.01 (Different Classification), 8.21.02 (Recognized Divergent Subject Matter), or 8.21.03 (Different Search).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the appropriate conclusion paragraph to state that restriction is proper because the inventions are independent/distinct for the reasons given and there would be a serious burden on the examiner if restriction is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventors — correction of inventorship upon cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is reminded that upon the cancellation of claims to a non-elected invention, the inventorship must be corrected in compliance with 37 CFR 1.48(a) if one or more of the currently named inventors is no longer an inventor of at least one claim remaining in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request to correct inventorship under 37 CFR 1.48(a) must be accompanied by an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76) identifying each inventor by legal name and the processing fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i). This form paragraph must be included in all restriction requirements for applications having joint inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election and reply — traverse definition and reply requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Election is the designation of the particular one of two or more disclosed inventions that will be prosecuted in the application. A reply should be made to each point raised by the examiner’s action, and may include a traverse or compliance. A traverse of a requirement to restrict is a statement of the reasons upon which the applicant relies for his or her conclusion that the requirement is in error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a rejection or objection is included with a restriction requirement, applicant must also distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the examiner’s rejection or objection (see 37 CFR 1.111).

rubrics_metrics.name: Election fixed by action on claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Election becomes fixed when the claims in an application have received an action on their merits by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims originally presented and acted upon determine the invention elected by an applicant; in an RCE, claims presented and acted upon should be treated as provided in MPEP § 821.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election other than express (by originally presented claims, generic claims only, or cancellation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Election may be made in other ways than expressly in reply to a requirement: (a) by originally presented claims treated as original claims for restriction purposes; (b) where only generic claims are first presented and prosecuted and later species claims are presented, the examiner may require election of a single species; (c) by optional cancellation of claims leaving claims to one invention which are then acted upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these principles when determining which invention is considered elected in the absence of an explicit election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express election and traverse — reconsideration under 37 CFR 1.143
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant disagrees with the requirement for restriction, he may request reconsideration and withdrawal or modification of the requirement, giving the reasons therefor. In requesting reconsideration the applicant must indicate a provisional election of one invention for prosecution, which invention shall be the one elected if the requirement becomes final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement will be reconsidered on such a request. If the requirement is repeated and made final, the examiner will at the same time act on the claims to the invention elected.
